h1: The 6 Best SDI Video Switchers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best SDI Video Switchers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 SDI video switchers scored on SDI input count, streaming, ISO recording and control, from a basic 4x1 to ATEM Extreme ISO.
summary: The Blackmagic Design ATEM SDI Extreme ISO is the SDI switcher to buy for serious multi-camera work: eight 3G-SDI inputs, 10-bit HD switching and direct internet streaming. The Osee GoStream Duet 8 ISO matches it with four SDI and four 4K HDMI inputs. For a simple signal selector, the Wiistar 4x1 does one job for under $100. The rest depends on how many cameras you run.
intro: The usual SDI buying error is counting inputs and ignoring what the switcher does with them. A box with four SDI ports that only selects one at a time is a router, not a production switcher, and the gap in price reflects it. Real switchers add transitions, keying, recording of each camera and a way to stream, and which of those you need decides the right model.

We ranked six SDI switchers on the Primea framework, from a plain 4x1 selector to an eight-input streaming production unit. Scores weigh SDI input count, whether the unit streams or records, the control options, the build and the fit for small crews. Several listings are short on detail, so we mark what the page states and tell you what to verify before ordering.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM SDI Extreme ISO Live Stream Switcher Bundle with 8' Cable
products.verdict: Eight 3G-SDI inputs, 10-bit HD switching and internet streaming. The most capable switcher here.
products.description:
The ATEM SDI Extreme ISO is described as feature rich, with eight 3G-SDI inputs, 10-bit HD switching and multicamera live streaming to the internet. This listing is a bundle that includes an 8 foot cable, and it sits in the $500 and up bracket.

It takes first place for input count and scope. Eight SDI inputs cover a church, a classroom or a multi-camera event without adding a second box, and the ISO naming points to separate recording of camera feeds, which the Osee below also lists. Against the ATEM SDI Pro ISO, you get twice the inputs on paper. The Pro ISO tops out at four.

A fit for crews running several cameras. The caveat is that the listing gives few details on outputs and recording, so verify them before you buy.
products.idealFor: Multi-camera event, church and classroom crews who need many SDI inputs.
products.skipIf: You only use one or two cameras.

products.name: Osee GoStream Duet 8 ISO Live Streaming Video Switcher
products.verdict: Four 4K HDMI plus four SDI inputs, clean ISO recording and hardware RTMP streaming.
products.description:
Osee's Duet 8 ISO features four 4K HDMI inputs and four physical SDI inputs. The listing says it records clean individual feeds from every source and streams directly from the hardware over RTMP to major platforms. It sits in the $500 and up bracket.

The mix of input types is the draw. Many small productions use SDI on long cable runs and HDMI for a laptop or a mirrorless camera nearby, and this box takes both without converters. It ranks second behind the ATEM Extreme because it offers four SDI inputs against the ATEM's eight, so it fits fewer SDI-only rigs.

Best for a studio mixing broadcast-style SDI cameras and HDMI sources. The caveat is that only four of the eight inputs are SDI.
cons: Less SDI scale than the ATEM
products.idealFor: Studios mixing SDI cameras with HDMI sources in one box.
products.skipIf: You need more than four SDI inputs.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM SDI Pro ISO Live Stream Switcher (SWATEMMXEPBPRISO)
products.verdict: Four 3G-SDI inputs and direct ethernet streaming. The sensible ATEM for smaller productions.
products.description:
The ATEM SDI Pro ISO offers four 3G-SDI inputs and lets you stream directly via ethernet. The listing also points to built-in production management. It falls in the $500 and up bracket.

It is the sensible half-step down from the Extreme. You keep the ATEM approach and the streaming, but with four SDI inputs instead of eight, which is enough for most two-to-three camera shoots. It ranks third because the Extreme gives you headroom for the same family of controls, and the Osee Duet 8 ISO adds HDMI. The listing also gives fewer details than we would like.

A fit for small crews who want ATEM streaming. The caveat is that four inputs leave no room to grow.
products.idealFor: Small crews running two or three SDI cameras with streaming.
products.skipIf: You expect to add more cameras later.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM SDI Live Production Switcher (SWATEMMXEP)
products.verdict: A broadcast-style SDI switcher with ethernet control and a USB-C 2.0 interface.
products.description:
The ATEM SDI Live Production Switcher is described as delivering pristine broadcast visuals from SDI inputs, with ethernet control and a USB Type-C 2.0 interface. It is in the $200 to $500 bucket, below the ISO models.

The lower price is the point. This is the cheaper ATEM, with the same family of controls and no ISO tag in its name, which suggests it does not record individual feeds the way its siblings do. That keeps it fourth. Ethernet control lets a laptop or a hardware panel run the switching, a useful option for a crew that wants the operator away from the rack.

A fit for a live production that needs switching but not isolated recordings. The caveat is that the listing gives a short feature list, so check recording and streaming support before ordering.
products.idealFor: Live productions that need switching and remote control without ISO recording.
products.skipIf: You must record each camera separately.

products.name: Osee GoStream Duet Multiple Camera SDI and HDMI Live Stream Video Mixer Switcher
products.verdict: A multi-camera SDI and HDMI live stream mixer with key effects and several control methods.
products.description:
Osee's GoStream Duet is a multiple camera SDI and HDMI live stream mixer. The listing highlights an enriched input selection, multiple control methods, and a rich set of key effects and transitions. Pricing is in the $200 to $500 range.

Fifth place follows from how much it asks you to take the mixer features on trust. The listing gives no input counts or streaming specifications, so it is harder to place against the Duet 8 ISO, which prints four SDI and four HDMI inputs. What it offers is a lower price than the ISO model, along with the same hybrid SDI and HDMI approach and a strong set of effects.

Choose it for a smaller hybrid setup. The caveat is the missing input count.
products.idealFor: Smaller hybrid setups that mix SDI and HDMI cameras.
products.skipIf: You need to know the exact input count before buying.

products.name: Wiistar 4x1 3Gb/s SDI Switcher with ReClock Technology
products.verdict: A four-in, one-out SDI selector that auto-switches between SD, HD and 3G-SDI. A router, not a mixer.
products.description:
Wiistar's 4x1 takes four SDI inputs to one output and switches automatically between SD, HD and 3G-SDI signals. It supports multiple video resolutions and uses ReClock technology to regenerate the signal. Expect to spend $50 to $100.

Last place is down to category, not quality. There are no transitions, no streaming and no recording, so it cannot replace the ATEM or Osee units above. As a plain four-to-one selector for a monitor, a recorder or a projector, though, it is the cheapest way to choose between SDI sources, and the signal regeneration helps keep long cable runs clean.

Best for someone who needs to pick among SDI feeds without production features. The caveat is that it cannot mix, record or stream.
products.idealFor: Anyone who needs to choose among SDI feeds on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want to cut between cameras with transitions or stream.

whatMatters.detail: Each camera needs its own input, and extra inputs leave room for graphics or a laptop. The ATEM Extreme lists eight 3G-SDI inputs, the Pro ISO four, and the Wiistar four in and one out. Count your cameras today, add two for growth, and check the listing states a number, because a graphics laptop or a replay source also needs a port.

ISO means each camera feed is recorded separately alongside the program, so you can re-edit later. The Osee Duet 8 ISO says it records clean feeds from all sources, and the ATEM units carry ISO in their names. Look for explicit wording about recording individual inputs, not just a general record function, because only separate files let you fix a bad cut afterward in an editor.

Direct hardware streaming means the switcher sends video to a platform without a computer in between. The Osee lists hardware RTMP, and the ATEM Pro ISO lists streaming over ethernet. Check that the listing names the streaming method, and remember a stable wired connection matters more than the switcher, so test your upload speed at the venue before the event day.

Switchers run from the front panel, a computer over ethernet, a USB link or a hardware controller. The ATEM SDI lists ethernet control and USB Type-C 2.0, and the Osee Duet lists multiple methods. Decide who operates the unit and from where, then look for the interface that fits, since a switcher with no remote option forces the operator to sit beside the rack.

SDI comes in SD, HD and 3G flavours, and a switcher must support the one your cameras output. The Wiistar auto-switches among all three and the ATEM Extreme lists 10-bit HD. Check your camera's SDI output format against the listing, and note that 4K may need different hardware, so confirm the resolution before cabling a whole venue around one model.

howToChoose.intro: Count your SDI cameras first. It narrows the field faster than any feature.

faq.a: The listings are mixed. The Osee Duet 8 ISO names four 4K HDMI inputs, while the ATEM SDI models describe HD and 3G-SDI. Check the resolution on the specific input you plan to use.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying a selector when you need a mixer. The Wiistar 4x1 only chooses a source, so you cannot dissolve between cameras or add graphics. If you cut live, start with an ATEM or Osee.

faq.q: Is the ATEM Extreme worth it over the Pro ISO?
faq.a: Only if you need more than four cameras. The Extreme lists eight 3G-SDI inputs, while the Pro ISO lists four and costs less. For a two or three camera shoot the Pro ISO covers it.

faq.q: How do I connect cameras to an SDI switcher?
faq.a: Use BNC cables rated for your signal, connect each camera to an input and set the output format to match. For the Osee Duet 8 ISO, HDMI cameras go to the HDMI inputs instead.

faq.q: How do I keep the unit running reliably?
faq.a: Keep vents clear, use quality BNC cables and update firmware only between events. The Wiistar's ReClock helps long runs, and the ATEM units benefit from a wired ethernet link when streaming.

faq.q: Can I stream without a computer?
faq.a: Yes with some models. The Osee Duet 8 ISO streams over hardware RTMP and the ATEM SDI Pro ISO streams via ethernet. You still need a stable network connection and a destination platform account.

finalTake: The Blackmagic Design ATEM SDI Extreme ISO earns first place with eight 3G-SDI inputs, 10-bit HD switching and internet streaming. The Osee GoStream Duet 8 ISO is the pick for mixed SDI and HDMI rigs, and the ATEM SDI Pro ISO fits smaller crews. Use the Wiistar only as a selector, and verify gaps on the sparse listings first.
